Yes. The story uses subtext naturally, enriching its setting rather than feeling forced. The university’s description of a converted hospital as an “experimental residential community,” contrasted with mold and closed maintenance cases, suggests institutional indifference beneath reassuring language.

Subtext also deepens the relationships. When Lizzy asks Mira to edit her application—“Only grammar”—the narrow permission signals both damaged trust and a tentative reopening of their friendship. The final act of putting one bowl back quietly conveys Mira’s loneliness and her growing willingness to respect another person’s choices. These meanings emerge through ordinary actions rather than imposed symbolism.
